messages:
Maya Chen: hey, trying to get redwoodctl running on an M1 work laptop. `brew install redwoodctl` completed but I get permission denied when it tried to link to /usr/local/bin :facepalm:
Jun Park: on Apple Silicon brew prefix is /opt/homebrew, not /usr/local. try `brew --prefix` then add that path to $PATH or run `brew link --overwrite redwoodctl` if it created keg-only files
Maya Chen: ahhhh yep that fixed the link. now redwoodctl login opens my browser but then my terminal says `failed to read token from keychain`
Alex Rivera: mac keychain prompt sometimes blocks headless flows. you can do `redwoodctl login --device-code` to paste a code instead of waiting for a browser pop. works well in tmux
Priya Nair: FYI if you're on WSL the browser flow is useless. use `redwoodctl login --headless` or device-code. BUT also watch out: tokens end up in the Windows credential manager by default, and WSL processes can't access it unless you configure credential sharing
Maya Chen: were seeing another weirdness: after login returns I immediately run `redwoodctl local serve --profile=dev`, but the serve command still says "no active credentials"
Jun Park: that's a race we've hit. the login call writes to keychain/credential store asynchronously. local serve reads credentials synchronously right away. add a small sleep or run `redwoodctl auth status --profile=dev` to confirm before starting
Maya Chen: example output I got:
```
$ redwoodctl config list
PROFILE  STORE   LAST_LOGIN
default  keychain  2026-10-03T15:12:10Z
dev      keychain  <none>
```
Maya Chen: config shows dev not populated even though browser said success
Alex Rivera: repro: login --profile=dev returns success HTTP 200 but the credential helper exits with code 0 before keychain commits. workaround in scripts: poll `redwoodctl auth status` until it returns ok, or invoke `sleep 1`
Priya Nair: another WSL-specific pain: `redwoodctl local serve` uses the profile store set in config (~/.config/redwoodctl/config.yaml). Windows user-land defaults to keychain/credential manager. You can force file store: `redwoodctl login --profile=dev --store=file --file-path=/home/<user>/.config/redwoodctl/creds.json` then both WSL and Windows will read the same file if you mount it
Maya Chen: adding that to onboarding doc. also noticed on a fresh linux VM the installer script does `sudo mv redwoodctl /usr/local/bin` which fails when /usr/local/bin isn't writable in some distros. we should document non-sudo install (user bin)
Jun Park: filed an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/432 (installer: respect $PREFIX or --install-dir). small PR incoming to honor $HOME/.local/bin
dev-bot: new release v0.10.1 published — includes `--store=file` default toggle and a `--blocking` flag for login (CLI will wait until credential store commit completes)
Maya Chen: nice! that --blocking flag will help scripts a lot
Alex Rivera: one more oddity: `redwoodctl local serve --profile=dev --port 3000` sometimes ignores --profile when REDWOODCTL_PROFILE env var is unset. I think our config precedence logic is reversed for local serve
Priya Nair: opened a bug for precedence: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/435. short-term: set the env var `export REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=dev` in your terminal before local serve
Maya Chen: thanks y'all — will update the internal onboarding checklist with device-code, headless, file-store examples and a note about the blocking flag :thumbsup:
Jun Park: glhf. ping me if you want a quick pairing session to update the install script
Alex Rivera: :rocket:
Priya Nair: :eyes:
